Cite the specific evidence (the 'yeah, so that's kind of the idea' close vs the clean recommendation line). Name the ONE lever (commit to the final sentence) and give one testable move. Do NOT reduce 'authoritative' to a percentage or a score, and do NOT declare him ready.
badAnswerExample: You're about 80% of the way there! Based on your data, your scores are trending up. Keep practicing and work on sounding more confident — you'll get there. The key insight is consistency.
excellentAnswerExample: Closer than the fillers make you feel — your mechanics are already in range. The gap isn't the ums, it's the close. Yesterday you nailed the point ('consolidate the two vendors by Q3') then undercut it with 'yeah, so that's kind of the idea.' That last sentence is where authority leaks out. Next rep: state the recommendation, then stop on it — no softener after. That tests whether the point can stand without you apologising for it.
